description: Set a Rust project's version to an exact value in every place it must agree — a single crate or a Cargo workspace (e.g. a command-line tool scaffolded by `iru-setup-rust-cli`, a library, a multi-crate workspace). Rewrites the root `Cargo.toml` `[package] version` and/or `[workspace.package] version` (which every member declaring `version.workspace = true` inherits), the `[package] version` of any other publishable member that moves in lockstep with it, and the `version = "…"` requirement of every path dependency on those packages (`[workspace.dependencies]`, `[dependencies]`/`[dev-dependencies]`/`[build-dependencies]`/`[target.….dependencies]`, inline or `[dependencies.<name>]` tables, keeping an `=`/`^`/`~` operator) — so `cargo` can still resolve the workspace after a `-dev` → release → next `-dev` cycle; tooling members with `publish = false` (e.g. `xtask`) or their own version are reported and left alone. Refreshes `Cargo.lock` with `cargo update --workspace --offline`, which rewrites only the workspace's own entries. Validates the value as SemVer 2.0 (what Cargo requires) and follows this catalog's `x.y.z-dev` development-version convention (Step 5). Uses an embedded, tested Python helper (driven by `cargo metadata`, regex-based TOML edits that keep comments, formatting and CRLF line endings) with `--list` and `--dry-run` modes, and refuses to write when the version locations disagree until the user confirms. Invoke as `/iru-rust-bump-version <new-version>` where `<new-version>` is the literal target (e.g. `1.4.0` or `1.5.0-dev`) — this skill never computes a bump itself (`iru-release` computes the release/next-dev values per Step 5 and passes each one through). Also accepts `args` (`key: value` lines): `sync-files: yes|no` (default: ask) to also update README/Antora version mentions (`cargo install <crate> --version`, `<crate> = "x.y.z"` dependency snippets, `cargo add <crate>@x.y.z`, "Latest release" markers, `docs/antora.yml`), `next-version: <upcoming-version>` so that sync maps "Latest release" markers to `<new-version>` and "Current development version" markers to the upcoming value, and `dry-run: yes|no` (default `no`) to print the diff without writing anything. Reports every location found with its old value, the new value, and every file touched. Use whenever the user, or `iru-release` (key `rust`), needs a Rust project's version set to a specific value instead of hand-editing `Cargo.toml` files.
